title: Flash Sale Inventory: Lock Duration vs Oversell Risk

steps.prompt: During a flash sale, hundreds of buyers a minute check out against 40 Product inventory records. Each checkout calls an external payment gateway that takes 3–8 seconds to authorize before stock is decremented, and no unit may be sold twice. Which concurrency pattern should the architect use?

options.label: Add a version field to inventory rows and compare it when saving each decrement
options.rationale: Optimistic locking records when data was read and, at save, checks whether someone else changed the record in the interim, sending the writer back for the latest version. No lock stays open during the 3–8 second gateway call, and a buyer who loses the race re-reads stock instead of overselling.

options.label: Query the inventory rows with SOQL FOR UPDATE before calling the payment gateway
options.rationale: FOR UPDATE keeps the row locked until the transaction ends, so every buyer of that product queues behind a 3–8 second gateway call and waiting transactions fail with lock errors.

options.label: Keep stock counts in Platform Cache and reconcile them to the records on a schedule
options.rationale: Platform Cache has no row locking or transactions, so two buyers can read the same last unit and both sell it before the scheduled reconciliation runs.
